reason: Survives the schedule/feasibility lens. The core of the idea is a finals choice among files that are already scored. It needs no GPU, no LB slot, no friend A, no quota reset and no Kaggle dataset. exp52 was scored 0.950 as #32 at 07:50 UTC 25 Sep (CONTEXT.md l.1494-1498). The x138-family candidates #34 exp56 (id 56545267) and #35 exp57b (id 56545786) were submitted on 25 Sep and are expected 17:00-20:00 UTC (CONTEXT.md l.1506-1527). That is ~3.5 days before the 29 Sep 10:00 UTC information deadline. The only mandatory work is 0.3-0.5 h of container time to write the rule into CONTEXT.md before #34/#35 score, plus the user ticking two boxes by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC. P(implemented as described in time) ~0.95. The E[D+] numbers check out (python): mu -0.002/s 0.004 -> +0.00079 (Phi 0.31); s 0.006 -> +0.00153; mu -0.003/s 0.004 -> +0.00052; s 0.006 -> +0.00119. The value verdict argues s is realistically 0.002-0.004, because exp52 and x138 share detector, head, edge network and ILP. That puts the premium at +0.00006..+0.0005, which is a value issue and not a schedule issue. The optional 'guard-safe F1' part is also feasible on the schedule. Build the deadline patch 0.5-2 h in the container on 25 Sep. Do the dummy run on vitaliineibauer GPU right after the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC reset (15-40 min). Submit ~00:30-01:00 UTC 26 Sep; it scores ~08:00-11:00 UTC 26 Sep (the x138-type run needs 7-10 h of latency, inside the 12 h limit). That leaves >= 2 days of slack. It is needed only if latency(#34/#35) >= 7.5 h, and it costs 1 of 21 slots plus the user's OK. Two schedule holes must be patched (see fix). (a) If #34 < 0.953 (environment mismatch), F1 falls back to exp51/exp52. Then 'F2 = exp52' makes F2 a byte-level twin of F1 (a float-only diff, public tie), and the hedge is wasted. (b) If the user does not tick by 29 Sep 20:00, Kaggle auto-selects the two best public files, i.e. the two x138 near-copies (exp57b + exp56). That is exactly the outcome the idea wants to avoid.
fix_if_any: Pre-register a complete decision table in CONTEXT.md before 17:00 UTC 25 Sep. (1) #34 >= 0.952 and #35 >= #34 + 0.001 -> F1 = exp57b; else if #34 >= 0.952 -> F1 = exp56 (tie within 0.001 -> exp57b only if its lab division check was positive). F2 = exp52 if public(exp52) >= public(F1) - 0.003..0.004, else the scored x138-family file with the most different tail. (2) If #34 < 0.952 or errors -> F1 = exp51 (not exp52: keep the integer file, since float is a public tie), and F2 = the best scored x138-family file (exp56/exp57b), NOT exp52. (3) Latency gate: if the submit->score latency of the chosen x138 F1 is >= 7.5 h, F2 = exp52 whatever the public gap, and optionally submit the guard-safe rebuild at 26 Sep ~00:30 UTC (scored by ~11:00 UTC 26 Sep). (4) Schedule a reminder for the user at 29 Sep ~12:00 UTC (send_later, human_request only if the user asks; otherwise note it in the RESUME block) to tick F1/F2 by hand, because the Kaggle auto-selection picks two near-copies. (5) Any later file that beats F1 by >= 0.002 replaces F1 by the same table. F2 is never re-chosen by public score among near-copies, and exp52 is never re-tuned.
realistic_public_gain: 0 by construction (a choice among scored files).
realistic_private_gain: +0.00006..+0.0015 expected score premium (s 0.002-0.006, mu -0.002..-0.004; s is a guess, and the value verdict favours the low end, ~+0.0003 over a near-copy F2). Larger rank value if the x138 copy cluster (41 teams at 0.953) moves together on private. Up to ~+0.005..+0.01 only if the x138 repair guard fired on private-only datasets, which latency(#34) < 7.5 h rules out for free.
critical_path: 1) agent-container: write the pre-registered decision table (above) into CONTEXT.md RESUME/FINALS block, 0.3-0.5 h, 25 Sep 11:30-12:30 UTC, before any #34/#35 score (earliest ~17:00 UTC). 2) Kaggle scores #34/#35 ~25 Sep 17:00-20:00 UTC; the user or agent records the scores and the submit->score latencies. 3) Conditional, only if latency >= 7.5 h: container builds the x138 deadline patch 25 Sep 20:00-22:00 UTC; vitaliineibauer Kaggle GPU dummy run 26 Sep 00:05-00:45 UTC (after the quota reset); the user OKs and submits ~00:45 UTC; scored ~08:00-11:00 UTC 26 Sep (well before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC). 4) Apply the table to any later file that beats F1 by >= 0.002, up to the last informative submission (29 Sep 10:00 UTC, scored ~17:00-20:00 UTC). 5) The user ticks F1/F2 by hand by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC (reminder at ~12:00 UTC). No friend A, no Colab, no dataset upload. The only shared resource is one optional slot on 26 Sep.
